utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. McCloskey, are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning, Mr. President, we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. McCloskey: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Butler. Yesterday you were talking about prisoner responsibilities, and you had discussed one document. Could you go to the next document you've chosen, I believe it's Exhibit 408.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is a Drina Corps document which takes the general guidance that's found in the regulations and puts it into more specific form. And as you can tell from the header information, it's to be sent to the commands of all brigades and all the separate units of the Drina Corps. What I'd like to highlight in this document is starting at the second paragraph where it reflects that from the moment they are captured, enemy soldiers who are put out of action must be treated as prisoners of war in accordance with the Geneva Conventions. It also notes several sentences down that in addition to criminal responsibility, persons acting in this way also incur other types of responsibility. The responsibility rests not only with the immediate perpetrators of criminal offenses and inhumane treatment but also by their superior officers because prisoners of war are not the property of individuals or military units, but the responsibility of the VRS and the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, in your review of the material, did you -- have you found any reliable indications that the Muslim men that were detained in Potocari and detained in Bratunac on 12, 13, 14 July were ever not the responsibility of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you want to say anything else on this document?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just moving to the last paragraph, notwithstanding the practical applications of the Geneva Conventions, it is also noted by the leadership of the Drina Corps that one of the reasons why they're doing this is because they're demanding that their prisoners of war be treated in the same manner, because obviously during this period Bosnian Serb soldiers had been captured by Bosnian Muslims and this is one of the major tenets of the prisoner of war treatment. Just to finish, the document signed by the deputy commander chief of staff of the Drina Corps at the time, Colonel Skocajic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what's the next document you've got on this topic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, based on this order of 15 July, two days later, the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade command publishes its own instructions on the treatment of prisoners of war. Moving to the third paragraph, it again notes the fact that according to these provisions, enemy soldiers who are rendered unfit for battle by wounding or surrendered by laying down their weapons are considered prisoners of war from the moment of capture. It reiterates in the next paragraph that, again, prisoners of war are not the responsibility of any one individual or unit but of the Army of Republika Srpska and Republika Srpska itself. And it also notes that in addition to the direct perpetrators of criminal offenses in inhuman acts, superior officers in their unit will also bear any such responsibility. It specifically indicates that the brigade command should be informed when prisoners are taken and that the military police requested to take over the prisoner. It also specifies that wounded prisoners should be transported to the health centre as soon as possible, receive medical treatment and the brigade should be informed of this. The last paragraph on this page reflects the fact that while staying at the military police as the responsibility of the security organs, they should be provided with the accommodation and human conditions and treated in accordance with the provisions of international law. And finally other than the that officials interviewing the prisoners and those in charge of their security, other individuals should be denied access. This, of course, is to safeguard the prisoners. On this last page, again it reflects the fact that Serbian citizens and soldiers are being held captive by the other side and their treatment is reciprocal. The last paragraph, inform all members of units as to how to treat prisoners of war, immediately inform the brigade command of any violations of the provisions. And it is signed by the commander at the time, Colonel Vuksic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Butler, on the brigade level if large amounts of prisoners are taken, such as in this case, the prisoners stored in Bratunac on the 12th, 13th, 14th of July, what unit in a brigade command structure would normally be -- would share in the responsibility for feeding and caring for the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when you're looking at it in a brigade and a situation, particularly where -- one where you have several hundred prisoners as a minimum number, it is an activity that touches on almost every aspect of the brigade staff. As I noted earlier, the security branch has primary responsibility in sharing the security of the prisoners, the rear services branch has responsibility in feeding the prisoners, attending to their medical care. Certainly in the specific case of the Bratunac Brigade which has a military police platoon of only 30 people, the brigade command is going to have to delegate or designate other units to guard the prisoners. It's a 24-hour job and you're going to have to rotate your people, clearly. So in this particular instance the treatment of prisoners of war, above the one or two or five number issue is going to be an activity that is going to involve significant parts of the brigade staff and components of the command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If the rear services was providing no food support and they were providing no medical support for hundreds and hundreds of prisoners over a two-day period, in your opinion would the commander of that brigade be aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given the scope of number of prisoners and the fact that they weren't being cared for, I would find it very unlikely that the brigade commander could not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point, I don't mean to interrupt, and I haven't objected, I don't believe that the form of the questions are proper because they assume facts not in evidence. Now, if the gentleman wishes to state that all those prisoners were the responsibility or belonged to the Bratunac Brigade, then I would like to hear testimony. But the form of the question that was initially posed by the Prosecutor assumes that all these prisoners belong to the Bratunac Brigade. I didn't object in light of yesterday's rulings from the Court, but I do think that a foundation needs to be laid so that at least we know what this gentleman's opinion is. Whose prisoners are all these thousands of people or hundreds or thousands or whatever the number may be that they're talking about. Unless he's differentiating numbers from the Bratunac Brigade that were captured at some point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I understand that this witness is an expert witness. The expert witness is entitled to draw some conclusions in his testimony. I think this is only the witness's opinions or conclusions on this particular matter. I agree with you that it is an important issue in this case. Mr. Karnavas, you have the full right to cross-examine this witness at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. McCloskey, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One final issue, if I could, on this particular document, is again noting its date of 17 July. And certainly this document would have been in effect several months afterwards when we have information that Colonel Blagojevic was the acting chief of staff of the unit at the time. So this is certainly an instruction that as the acting chief of staff he would have been aware of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's change gears again as we -- in the chronological narrative that we are going through. Can we -- can you give us the briefest background as we approach the actual attack on the Srebrenica enclave, and I noticed you've picked Exhibit 410, a Drina Corps order dated 6 July, exhibit -- yes, 410.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: By way of a quick background, the attack, while it was initially planned to commence early on the 4th or 5th of July, in fact, began on the morning of the 6th of July. And as much of the evidence that's in my report indicates, the attack started off well, there was some resistance. But by the 6th of July, the units involved in Krivaja 95 were relatively decisively engaged in combat and were moving forward rather successfully. What this document does represents a report from the Drina Corps IKM, or forward command post to the commands of the brigades, one ordering the continuation of attacks and updating where the units have reached their positions for the day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just concentrate on what the Bratunac Brigade was doing according to this document, if anything.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In paragraph 4, the fourth bullet notes that with support, forces in contact, the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, and in this case we're not talking about the entire brigade, just those auxiliary forces which we've talked about yesterday, is taking over the Divljakinja area and shall be ready to continue the attack towards Gradac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can you continue your brief through to this time frame and just giving us the highlights so we can have a background as we approach the fall of the enclave, specifically concentrating on what the Bratunac Brigade is doing and anything you have about the commander of that brigade.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, moving to Exhibit P411, reflecting what the Bratunac Brigade is doing during that period, is the daily combat report for the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. And it again notes that they're conducting fire support activities. And in paragraph 2 reflecting that the brigade commander is at the IKM in Pribicevac and notes that the chief of staff and the staff are at the observation post of the 2nd Infantry Battalion. One of the things I would like to highlight that we discussed yesterday, on the handwritten version of the draft report, and I noted where we talk about an instance where the commander was signed or an individual signed for him, and I just wanted to illustrate where you have the "za," and then you have the signature of another officer. In this particular instance it's Lieutenant Micic, who is an operations officer of the brigade, and he is designated to sign for the commander on the daily combat reports. There is another daily combat report on 7 July. It is Prosecution Exhibit 412. Again, in paragraph 2 notes the location of the brigade commander in the 3rd Infantry Battalion command post and the brigade chief of staff at the observation post of the brigade command. Moving on to 8 July, paragraph 2 again noting the location of the brigade commander. And noting that other officers are located in battalion command posts. And this reflects back to the Bratunac Brigade daily reports log that we discussed earlier, noticing that the brigade commander wanted elements of his brigade staff at the battalion command post to ensure activities are being carried out, as per directive. And this is Prosecution Exhibit 413. This is Prosecution Exhibit now 414. And as we discussed in my previous testimony and it's in my report as well, we've highlighted as a result of the operational directives, particularly 7 and 7.1 that the objective was not to ever take the urban area of Srebrenica, but it was to separate the Srebrenica and Zepa enclaves and to compress the safe area for the Srebrenica enclave into the urban area itself. On 9 July, based on the success of military operations to date, the president of the Republika Srpska, as of course the supreme commander, changes the direction of the operation and now directs that the operation is to actually capture and occupy the very town of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, we didn't go over it, but in the Krivaja 95 attack plan, was there any section that mentioned the possibility of further activities and the objectives noted to separate and reduce the enclave?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe so, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any section that or any comments about going forward if the chances arose?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was in the op plan. They were to be prepared to take advantage of a situation, but in this particular instance, I don't anticipate that anyone had anticipated the success of the operation was going to go and be as successful to actually lead to this as rapidly as it did. The reason why I'll note that is when you see events in future days, it becomes clear that the VRS did not anticipate the success of its own military operation as fast as it occurred and the events that occur afterwards. This particular document is signed General Tolimir, and of course he is the assistant commander for intelligence and security at the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I note this document in paragraph 4 insists that the UNPROFOR members and Muslim civilian populations be guaranteed safety in the event they cross over to the territory of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir. It also notes that they're banning the torching of residential buildings, again in light of the fact that they want to be able to occupy the area themselves now and don't want to have to rebuild the city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what's the next document in the narrative?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Prosecution Exhibit 415. This is the 9 July daily combat report, so it's the same day. And again it notes that the commander of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade is still at the IKM in the 3rd Battalion area. It reflects that the chief of staff is in the 1st Battalion area and that other officers of the brigade command are at the IKMs of the 1st, 2nd, and 4th Battalion. One issue I would like to highlight also is paragraph number 5 where we see one of the constant occurrences there is a result of the minefields and everything else laid. Soldiers are getting injured on mines and the location of minefields becomes a priority issue further down the line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And paragraph 7 talks about 15 UNPROFOR soldiers fled to the RS territory and were brought into the brigade command and then put up at the Hotel Fontana. Do you have any information concerning that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, notwithstanding the testimony of Captain First Class Nikolic at the time, we do have references in the military police log of the Bratunac Infantry Brigade that the military police do, in fact, have the good job of guarding the soldiers at the Hotel Fontana during this period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those soldiers used in any way in the discussions between the VRS command and the UN command?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- on the 11th of July when the NATO airforce at the direction of UNPROFOR started bombing VRS positions just outside of Srebrenica, those soldiers were effectively threatened with execution if the UNPROFOR and NATO did not stop the bombing of VRS soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why UNPROFOR soldiers might have fled to the RS territory at around this time as opposed to going back through Muslim territory?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, particularly on 9 July and afterwards, there was a significant amount of resentment by the members of the 28th Division and the Bosnian Muslims in general that the Dutch Battalion and UNPROFOR did not protect them as they saw their mandate to be. And, in fact, was falling back and giving up territory. As a result, in a lot of cases, the Dutch Battalion soldiers felt safer putting themselves in the custody of the VRS as opposed to trying to withdraw back through Bosnian Muslims lines. I believe one case on the 9th that is borne out by the fact that a Dutch soldier is killed by grenade fragments thrown by a Bosnian Muslim soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go on to the 10th of July. I believe the next document you've chosen is Exhibit 417, a 10 July daily combat report on the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry this is Prosecution Exhibit 416.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: And it is the daily combat report from 10 July 1995. Looking at paragraph 2, again it notes where the brigade commander is, where the brigade chief of staff is, and the rest of the commanding officers are at observation posts, according to plan. It also, for the first time, reflects the physical presence on the ground in the brigade zone of General Mladic, who of course is the commander of the VRS, Major General Zivanovic, who is the Drina Corps commander. It notes the continuing presence of Major General Krstic, as well as the commanders of other corps level brigades who are participating. Paragraph 5 notes that individual named Sreten Petrovic, who is the deputy commander of the 3rd Battalion, suffered serious injuries in his thigh and forearm. And in this instance, then Lieutenant Petrovic was one of the officers leading the Bratunac Brigade's auxiliary attack in support of the main operation. As it turns out, his injuries are not as serious as reported and within several days he is back on duty. As a component of General Mladic being on the ground there, an order is given by General Mladic that is Worker's Battalion or all people eligible for compulsory work are to be mobilised and are to report to the brigade headquarters by 1800 hours on 10 July. And as we've noted before, this is an instance where an authorised staff officer signs for the brigade commander. Again, in this particular case it is Major Eskic who is the chief of personnel services for the brigade, and if you look just under the brigade stamp there you can see the "za." At this particular time we'll go back to this document which is labelled Prosecution Exhibit 386. While the army is attempting to mobilise as much manpower as possible, at the same time police units are being designated to also go to Bratunac. And I believe we've discussed this document in detail earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So let's now go to 11 July.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the 11 July daily combat report for the Bratunac Brigade. And while Srebrenica, the town itself, actually came under VRS control approximately 1500 hours on 11 July, because of the drafting of the report and when it was sent, it's not reflected in this. However, it does note that the NATO airforce was active on a few occasions and that the brigade commander in paragraph 2 is still in the 3rd Battalion area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what area is Pribicevac in, which battalion area?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the 3rd Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, for the sake of the record, please identify the number of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sorry. That was 419.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: July 11th, daily combat report. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Butler, have you reviewed the video of General Mladic and others going through Srebrenica on 11 July?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I'm familiar with that video.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall the -- at one point in the video, General Mladic is surrounded by some of his brigade commanders and others and says, "On to Potocari, on to Bratunac." And then Vinko Pandurevic enters in briefly and says, "But we need to take the hills," something to that effect?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On 11 July, did the VRS actually follow General Mladic's orders and actually take Potocari?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, they did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what -- how far did they get? Where did their positions consolidate at the end of the evening of 11 July, the VRS, that is?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The VRS by 11 July had managed to consolidate their positions from the Srebrenica area just beyond the town of Srebrenica and into the hills above the town. One of the problems that had occurred is that on the 10th of July, the forces of the Bosnian Muslim 28th Division made a decision to break contact and to attempt to begin a withdrawal towards the Tuzla area. This fact was not known to the VRS at the time. When you look at that video and you have General Mladic exhorting his brigade commanders to move on immediately to Potocari, what happens after that is his brigade commanders meet in counsel and discuss with General Mladic and reflect the fact that they've lost contact with the 28th Infantry Division, and that it would not be prudent to move forward until they knew where it was and what it was doing. So as I understand it, General Mladic relented to that point and they spent the evening in and around the Srebrenica area making plans to continue offensive operations on the morning of the 12th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your study and analysis, do you have any indications where the VRS first thought the Muslim 28th Division folks were?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this point in time, the VRS decided or determined that the most likely spot for the 28th Division was that they would have withdrawn into an area of -- that the Srebrenica or former enclave known as the Bardera triangle, which is roughly south-west of Srebrenica. And a very hilly area which UNPROFOR had not normally been permitted access to. So during the evening of the 11th, the plans were made, and on the morning of the 12th, the bulk of the VRS's military forces began sweep operations of that area. In fact, the Bosnian Muslim forces of the 28th Infantry Division did not go into that area at all and instead were withdrawing to the Jaglici area where they were going to prepare for their breakout towards Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By the early morning hours of 12 July did the VRS start to get some indications of where the Muslims were really going?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, they did. As the evidence will indicate, units that were on the north and west side of the enclave opposite Susica and opposite Jaglici were starting to pick up indications that there was a large body of Muslim men in that area and that they were beginning to break through the minefields there. What you see in a series of intercepts is the reports by these units that they're seeing hundreds of men in an area that they were not anticipating. And the flow of information from that lowest level until it ultimately reaches the leadership of the VRS in Bratunac at that time, unfortunately for the VRS too late for them to be able to change the activities of the army that they had planned that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go through some of those intercepts and documents about the column, and I believe the first one is Exhibit 420, an intercept from 12 July at 056 hours?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry this one is 0656 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, 0656 hours. What can you make of this intercept?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, technically the two subscribers are unidentified, but from the context of the conversation you can clearly tell that subscriber X is passing information on groups of hundreds of individuals and the route that they're taking. It also talks about that one of the problems that they're having is that the route that is being taken is a gap that has existed between the deployed forces of the Milici Light Infantry Brigade and the deployed forces of the Bratunac Infantry Brigade. And already the army is discussing whether or not there are forces available from the MUP that can be used to plug that gap.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just briefly describe for the Court where the areas of Bokcin Potok and Kamenica and Pobodje are? What is that general area as it relates to -- do you have that -- it's probably best that we just hand you that map again. And that is P85.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we can zoom in a little bit just on the Bratunac Brigade area. That's good. Just to, again, orient the town of Srebrenica, now this area right here just north of the Jadar River, there is the area that I previously referred to as the Bardera triangle area. This village complex of Jaglici and Susnjari, again at the north end of the former enclave at this time, and the areas in question that we're talking about are along this red line, these villages, it's roughly here. Now again, as I previously discussed, movement in this area is very hilly and, of course, it's dictated by terrain. The valley route that the column took was well known to the VRS, and as a result while they did not have actual forces in there, they had placed mines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This comment about, "They started passing through my battalion," what are the options for the battalions that could be?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this particular juncture, you have one wing of the Milici Battalion which begins here --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record, that's just west of the red line, the route of the column.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the other battalion in question is identified up here as the 4th Battalion of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And if you have nothing else to say about that, let's go to the next exhibit, 421.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can zoom out a little bit, please, on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: ELMO, ELMO, ELMO. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is intercept 12 July at 0740. Obrenovic is noted as one of the subscribers. And in the context of the conversation, recognising where this gap is and the police forces are starting to stream into that, one of the issues that is coming up is, of course, command and control and how to effectively communicate with them. And in this particular instance, the unidentified subscriber indicates that Mane, and in this instance we're talking about Mane Djuric, the deputy head of the CSB Zvornik, will call and that the police in Konjevic Polje have been told to the same as the engineering battalion are doing and that he can give orders to them through the commander of the Engineering Battalion. Again, the MUP is going to piggyback off of the communication's nodes of the Engineer Battalion that exists there nodes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you show us the map again, and remind us where the Engineering Battalion is.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Engineering Battalion is located right at the intersection of the Bratunac to Konjevic Polje road here, and it's located right at this intersection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And based on your analysis, what MUP forces were there that they may have been referring to in this intercept?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I had indicated in my narrative, back in March of 1995, because of continuing deployment of the VRS Drina Corps to other locations, some of the security of these key intersections or check areas, and in particular Konjevic Polje, as it was known to be an area where Muslims from the 28th Division exfiltrated out to Tuzla, some of the MUP units were assigned responsibility to patrol these areas. I believe in July of 1995, there are elements of the 5th PJP Company from CSB Zvornik that are providing a checkpoint and security at this intersection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this comment that he can give orders to them through the commander of the engineering battalion, does that tell us anything about command, who's commanding who?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it indicates that with respect to command that the army is the agency that is directing the operations of everyone in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you don't have any other comments on that intercept, can we go to the next exhibit, 422. And can you start with an explanation of the heading.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in this particular instance what you have is a conversation between the duty officer at Badem, and Badem is the telephonic code name of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, and Zlatar, which is the code name for -- the telephonic code name for the Drina Corps. And in this particular instance, the Drina Corps headquarters is requesting an information update as to the situation regarding the link with the neighbour on the right. And in this particular instance, in the context I believe that the neighbour on the right that they're referring to is the Milici Light Infantry Brigade. It also notes that X at Badem, Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, is noting that General Krstic is present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this is a 12 July intercept, is it not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when it says, "General Krstic, he is up there in his office," where do you think that would be?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: My analysis of that indicates that the command staff of the Drina Corps was using the headquarters of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade as their own forward command post of the Drina Corps. And that is a practice that is pretty well enshrined in the former JNA regulations as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could it mean that he's up there at the Pribicevac forward command post?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Potentially, but the phrase, "He is up there in his office," would argue against that. Further, the fact that it's the Badem duty officer, the Badem duty officer, assumably in this position has personal knowledge of the location of General Krstic, otherwise he wouldn't be saying where he is. He would have no way of knowing whether General Krstic was physically at the IKM or touring with the troops. So I think the balance of probabilities here is that General Krstic is physically at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There has been some testimony that there was a possible forward command post at the Hotel Fontana. What is your view on the possibility that this is a reference to General Krstic being at the Hotel Fontana?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe that's the case. Looking at the documents and falling back on even the testimony of the commander of the communications battalion of the Drina Corps during the Krstic trial, there is no evidence to suggest that a forward command post was established at the Hotel Fontana. There are a lot of practical military reasons why you wouldn't do that. First and foremost is the fact that all of the communications through the military already go through the Bratunac Brigade. And one of the most important functions of he command post, obviously, is the ability of a commander and his staff to be able to communicate with their subordinates and with their superiors. Had the VRS or had the Drina Corps made the decision to establish an operating command post at the Hotel Fontana, it would have required a significant upgrade in the ability or of the communications ability to be able to make that occur.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey, I'm sorry to interrupt you. Here we come across the intercept documents. For those documents to be admitted into the evidence, we need some background sources of those documents, so as to know the reliability of those documents. I wonder whether you could ask some questions to this witness concerning the source of those intercepts, or if not, I believe that we still need some corroboration evidence for those documents, the intercepts, to be admitted into the evidence. Because it seems to me that just a part of a notebook or something, we could not see the whole picture of those intercepts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I had Mr. Butler briefly describe that, but I can have him go into more detail on that. I thought you might have been tired of intercepts, but obviously they're an important piece of evidence and I understand. And I will ask him to go into that in more detail regarding his knowledge, so that as he discusses them you have a better feel for what he knows about them, as I understand your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And as Ms. Stewart reminds me, Your Honour, all these intercepts are intercepts that are in the two binders that we have chosen, just for your reference.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Butler, can you help us out, as Mr. Karnavas sometimes says, and give us a more detailed background about your knowledge of these particular intercepts. And let's start with -- well, the -- whether or not you studied the ability, the technical ability of the Bosnian Muslims to actually technically acquire the signals of these intercepts.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, starting at the beginning of the intercept story, as far as the OTP is concerned, I was with a group of other individuals actually at one of the sites and discussing the issue of collecting these intercepts. As part of my work there, trying to acquire intercept information that we believed was available, we were shown the wartime collection capabilities of the Bosnian Muslim army. Now, while I obviously can't get into great detail on the subject, as a military analyst, I do have a background in basic communications intelligence capabilities. And in fact, as an analyst, one of the requirements, at least within the U.S. military, is that it is the analyst who ultimately validates the reliability of the information coming from intercepts. So for me to be able to do that effectively, even in my own armed forces, I'm required to at least have a working background of basic communication intercept techniques, tactics, and the procedures. What I am -- again have a lot of confidence in is the fact that the Bosnian Muslim members of 2 Corps and the associated MUP people who were in the next office over understand and understood to a great detail the target environment upon which they were collected.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In an intelligence parlance or terminology, your -- as a collector, you're designated to go after a certain target. In this particular instance, the collectors of the Bosnian Muslim 2 Corps and the MUP were targeted against the multi-channel communications network of the VRS Drina Corps. In particular, two or three specific communications nodes or trunks where all communications went through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean by that, what is a communications node or trunk?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In multi-channel radio relays, it is not broadband communications. Multi-channel radio relay is in effect a UHF band transmission that is tried to make as directional as possible through the use of parabolic antennas. I don't want to get into a large discussion as to the radio frequency propagation of parabolic antenna, but what it effectively does is it allows you to channel the majority of the power in one particular direction, lending to clarity of communications between the two subscribers. Now, obviously the Bosnian Muslim collection sites were not located between those two and three trunks that were in existence where the communications went through, and were collecting off of what are known as side-lobe communications. Even with a parabolic antenna, while most of the radio frequency power goes to the front, you have a phenomena known as a side lobe or a back lobe where you have radiated energy that goes off the side of the antenna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to clarify, which side is using the parabolic antenna to power their communications?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be the VRS is using the parabolic antennas in order to focus their communications between their multi-channel nodes. So in this particular case, the collection equipment that the Bosnian Muslim 2 Corps had, at least in my experience, was adequate to be able to collect the signals that were emanating off of those antennas from the side. And in retrospect, the VRS communications people actually made it rather easy for them to do that. They did not take what in most militaries would be basic fundamental steps to protect their communications to the most possible degree. For example, in most prudent military situations, your communications equipment, you try and use terrain as much as possible to mask any excess signals that go out, make it harder for someone to collect. In this particular case with the VRS Drina Corps, instead they put the stuff on the highest mountains around ensuring that they could get clear reception, and in doing so they also provided a lucrative target environment for the BiH 2 Corps. So at the first level I'm satisfied as an analyst that the BiH 2 Corps collectors at both sites had the technical ability to collect the data.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, did you actually get to see the kind of equipment in your visit to one of the sites that the Bosnian Muslim army at least told you they were using?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We've heard it described as ham radio equipment. Can you briefly describe this equipment and why you believe it was capable of picking up these transmissions?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in fact, it was for the most part amateur short wave or ultrahigh frequency radios that were modified to collect on these frequencies. Talking to a number of the individuals, in fact they discussed the procedures where, in some cases, the radios were modified by cutting their own crystals in order to allow them to do this. Now, from a technical perspective, while it may very well seem amateurish, the reality is that radio communications is a technology that is almost 100 years old, it is not rocket science, and you know, 14-year-old kids cut their own crystals in countries all over the world to listen to radio. It's an ingenious engineering solution and it is a very low-tech one in order to meet the needs of the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, witness. I must confess that I could not fully understand all those technical terms.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: My question is very simple, and that is: Do you know where these three particular intercepts come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not particularly -- the intercepts that I use, as a general rule, come from either the Bosnian 2 Corps material or some of the MUP ones. For the most part, I used primarily Bosnian 2 Corps intercepts. I cannot tell you every time I lay an exhibit down whether, it came from the Okresanica site or the Konjuh site. I believe that the witnesses in front of me have, with respect, testified to that already. And as a result, for me as an analyst, what specific site that they actually originated from is not relevant to the actual internal context of the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one question on that. Were you present at Okresanica when the notebooks were discovered, or were you not present at that time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was present when the notebooks were discovered, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe that.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: After several hours of discussing the issue with the site commander, who was authorised to assist us in any way possible but was sure he didn't have such material, we asked for and gained permission to actually inspect some of the old records and vaults which they had. In the arms room of that facility where they keep their weapons, there was an old vault, nobody knew what was in it, they opened it up and what we found were, in a very haphazard manner, hundreds of notebooks. Clearly they had never been indexed. They had -- doesn't look, at least from my appearance, that they had been touched in years. And the site commander was actually quite surprised that he even had them, because it was his understanding that they had already been sent to Tuzla and the ABiH archives years ago. At that point, once we understood that they were there, we re-closed the safe and immediately obtained permission from our contacts in the ABiH 2 Corps to take the documents in toto or at least the books from June to December of 1995, since our mandate at the time was only to deal with issues relating to Srebrenica in 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The notebooks you're talking about, are those little almost square notebooks with pink elephants and children's school notebooks that the intercept operators wrote down the first transcriptions in?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, they are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just one last question on that subject: Were you familiar with the various statements that the intercept operators and supervisors originally gave in the investigation as well as the testimony that they provided at the Krstic trial?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you find any of -- any problems or significant errors in any of their -- in the testimony or investigation record of that material?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. No significant errors. Clearly in some of the text translations from various sites, there are minor discrepancies. And of course that is to be expected under the circumstances, at least my opinion. But I am -- as I said, I have a high degree of confidence because I've spent several years working the validation process of these intercepts. If I had any doubts to their authenticity, and again as I said, I would begin the process extremely skeptical. If I had any doubts about their authenticity and the fact that they are a reliable indicator of what was being collected at the time, they would not have been before the Court in the Krstic case and they wouldn't be before you now, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's been mention of Croatian intercepts that were captured in a search in Mostar. Have you, as the investigation team, been able to carefully evaluate and analyse that material?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That group or that batch of material of intercepts is primarily a series of intercepts that were seized by SFOR as a result of their own weapons collection and intelligence activity in Mostar. And it has to do with Croatian military or HVO intercepts of Bosnian Muslim and Bosnian Serb communications. We have reviewed that for the July 1995 and beyond process as part of one looking for information that would lead generally to Srebrenica, as well as our Rule 68 obligations. I don't believe that any of intercepts - there may be one or two - that have even some bearing to general issues of the Drina Corps at that time and nothing that's Rule 68. Again, as a matter of their ability to collect, the Drina Corps is the furthest location from where that collection was occurring. We're still learning much about how they did that. There are still other investigation teams who are presently doing activities are related to that, which I don't think I can discuss in public session. However, from sheer physical distance, the Drina Corps represented the least lucrative target for the Croatian army intercept operators, and as a result we see almost no traffic with respect to the Drina Corps during that period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as far as you know, the Srebrenica investigation has -- have they been able to study the material, the intercept operators of that Mostar material, as we have for this set of Bosnian 2 Corps intercepts?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This particular investigation has not been able to do that with the operators from the Mostar collection. That is being accomplished, I understand, by their investigation teams for a different case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So have you used any of those materials in your analysis?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I have not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: A technical question, that is we have two pieces of intercepts that bear the same exhibit number. Can you give us an explanation on that. I think one with the 65 ter number is 894. The other is the 907, but they have the same exhibit number, that is 422/A.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Ms. Stewart may be the expert on that, Your Honour, and I'm sure we can sort that out at the break and make sure we clear that up properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's leave -- that was the last intercept of this grouping that we were talking about. And we are on July 12 going in a chronological order regarding the events of that day. Can you tell us what the next document you chose for your narrative, unless there's some other information you wanted to talk about in that intercept -- actually perhaps we haven't gotten to that intercept yet. I'm slightly confused. 422, let's talk about that.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a 12 July intercept at 1345 hours. And again it illustrates the fact that the duty operations officer Zlatar and another subscriber, which I believe is the Bratunac Brigade --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you believe that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the lower end of the text here where it says, "O," it indicates, "Please, I can just put you up there to General Krstic. He's in charge of the attack." General Krstic being at the Bratunac Brigade or in that area. Nothing of significance per se, but again a general continuation of the story that as the day wears on through 12 July 1995, the army in general and the duty officers and then subsequently the leadership of the Drina Corps and the other formations there are learning that the military threat posed by the column on the north side of the enclave is growing. And again, keeping in context that most of the manoeuvre forces at this time are engaged in sweeping operations at the south of the enclave in the Bardera triangle. So in simple terms, the most capable forces of the army are in the wrong place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Then switching gears from the intercepts of the 12th, let's get into some of the documents that you've chosen to help illustrate command-related issues, what various commands were informed of and informing others.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This particular document Prosecution Exhibit 423 is a 12 July 1995 report by the main office of the RS RDB, which is the Republika Srpska state security service to the deputy minister and the head of the public security department personally, and the head of the RS MUP in Bijeljina personally. What these reports are, are effectively intelligence reports collected by the security service and being passed up the MUP chain of command for the information of the political leadership. And what these reports indicate is the general knowledge of the security people from the state security service in and around Bratunac at the time pertaining to the situation with respect to the VRS, with the Dutch, and with the Bosnian Muslim civilians in and around Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What can you tell us about -- do you know the identities or the numbers of state security agents in the area of Potocari/Bratunac at this time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is my understanding that the investigation has learned and, in fact, have interviewed two individuals who we know were state security officers in the Bratunac at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what is you wanted to discuss in this document related to knowledge issues or command issues?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, and taking into account the time attributed to the reporting process, most of the information, even though this report is dated 12 July, pertains to events occurring on the 11th of July. And in the first paragraph it notes that they're aware that 20.000 Muslim refugees came into the UN Dutch headquarters in Potocari and they're also talking about another 60.000 refugees left Srebrenica for the north. Now, obviously that number is a bit inflated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how, just in your review of these documents from state security, how accurate are they? Relatively, not specifically?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, like all intelligence collectors, and in this particular case the people writing the report are intelligence collectors, they are reporting what they hear. At this particular level, they're not doing any analysing within context or validating information, they're just reporting the events on the ground as they hear them or understand them. So while their reporting is accurate, in a sense that the information that they're reporting is what they heard, it later becomes a judgement call as to just how accurate that information is in context with the other events. And there will be instances where they forward reports that are erroneous. In this particular case, I am not asking that the information on this report be relied on as the definitive answer of what was happening on the ground, however, I'm using these reports to provide an idea of what the general perception of events were as they were being reported by the RDB at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. The gentleman indicated that there were two state security officers on the ground. He didn't mention any names. I understand the Court's rulings, however, if I'm going to be cross-examining the gentleman, I should at least have advance notice as to who he's referring to so at least I can be prepared in my cross, as opposed to learning it on cross, asking him who were these officers and then having to dig through. Otherwise I'm going to be in a position of trying to find a needle in a hay stack. So if the gentleman is going to be making references as to information received from certain individuals, if he could reveal the names, and we can go into private session, but it would be very helpful and I think it would be helpful also to the Judges as well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, could you please be kind enough to give more information about names of those two persons. If you need, we could go to private session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't believe it's necessary. Right now I know the two individuals and I can't remember their names, and I can get their names over the break, sir, if that will make everyone -- it's not a problem at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I can give the names to Mr. Karnavas, no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I would like the names on the record, Your Honour, that's all. I appreciate the Prosecution's efforts to help us out here, but I would also like it on the record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll come back to that issue after the break. And we'll resume until quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey. I believe that those problems have been solved during the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. And I can fix the three that we've mistakenly given double numbers for on the record right now, I think, if you'd like me to. We had mistakenly used 420 for original Exhibit 179. We mistakenly used 421 as original Exhibit 181. And we mistakenly 422 as original Exhibit 185. Now, there will be other intercepts that were accidentally given a new number, and as we get those, we'll correct them as we go and we'll fix the whole thing tonight and get out a new list so we can change that and clear it up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Sorry, may I ask for a clarification. You said that 422 is original Exhibit 185. Which of the two 422s we have? Can you give the ERN number, because they are different. And there are different channels and times, so perhaps you can rely on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, I've got -- sorry, now I'm getting completely confused. I've got new numbers in front of me now, so maybe we just better fix this at the break. Now they're giving me new numbers and I apologise. It's my fault. We thought we had it organised and we apparently don't, I see. Janet will explain something very simple to me, I'm sure, but right now it's not registering very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Just in case, the two 422s we have, the two intercepts, one is the number -- the ERN number finished in 4936 and the other one whose got the same number here finished in 5897. So which one is the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Oh, I've got you now. You're using ERN numbers, you've got that all figured out. Good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The 936 ERN is the -- originally was the 185. And the 897 was originally P194. Now, are there other multiples -- that was the only multiple, so that fixes that and we'll fix it as we go. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Butler, let's now just clear up for the record, can you tell us now who the two state security people were that you believe were on the ground at the time.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. The name of one individual is Mr. Vitomir Tomic. And the second individual is named Sinisa Glogovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know whether or not any of these people were interviewed by the OTP?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Mr. Vitomir Tomic was interviewed by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, is there anything else you wanted to point out regarding Exhibit 423, that first 12 July state security report?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. That's good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And so we'll be going through the 12th of July, some of the documents of the various entities and commands to indicate flow of information and knowledge on this important day. What's the next exhibit you want to discuss?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit Number 424. It is another report from the Sarajevo RDB. And in this particular instance, just drawing the Court's attention to the first paragraph where it starts to become more broader knowledge concerning the issues of the column, what the army is doing, and I believe the third or fourth sentence it discusses the meetings on the evening 11 of July between the Muslim representatives under the mediation of UNPROFOR. Further down it notes that new negotiations are scheduled for the morning of the 12th and that the RDB is verifying reports of over 10.000 Muslims staying on the premises of the business companies in Potocari, guarded by UNPROFOR DutchBat units. It also raises the issue that given the fear of Muslim extremists and their attempts to break out, that the road between Pale and Zvornik might become vulnerable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. The Trial Chamber has seen some documents with time stamps or time indications at the end of them that give us some indication of the time of the document. Is there any way to figure out the time when this document was drafted or sent or received?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, there is not. There is not a time stamp on the original B/C/S version. And other than the date itself, the only indication of what time during the day that it might have been sent would have to be derived from our own empirical knowledge of what events were occurring on the ground that they're talking about in context.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when it says in the middle of that big second paragraph, "As a result new negotiations for scheduled for the morning of 12 July." What do you think that is a reference to?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again, I take that as an indication that this report or this piece of information was acquired and drafted out between the meetings at the end of 11 July, and with the knowledge that there are scheduled meetings on the 12th of July that have not yet occurred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what particular meeting do you think that is, if you do?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are the meetings, the two that occurred on the 11th between members of the VRS, the Dutch and the Bosnian Muslim representatives at the Hotel Fontana. And the meeting on the morning of 12 July, is in fact, what I call the third meeting of that series.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the next document in this series that you want to discuss.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Another one from 12 July, again moving on to generally set the framework of what people are aware of in the area, noting that on 12 July information that the RDB is getting from their sources is that the humanitarian situation is worse than ever. They estimate that 30.000 people in and around the Dutch Battalion base and also that a group of 8.000 are trying to reach the UNPROFOR base at Gornji Potocari. So a rough number of how many people are streaming into the Potocari area. One sentence in particular, "According to reports by military observers, there is not a single armed soldier of the so-called BH army among these people." In this context, I believe the military observers that they're talking about are information that they are gleaning from the UN military observers. It also talks about issues related to the last meeting on the 12th of July, 1995, where that the Dutch Battalion commander proposed that UNPROFOR provide 20 buses and complete the evacuation in rounds of a thousand people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go on to the next document and can you identify what this document is, what entity or organisation it's from. This is Exhibit 426.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. This is a series of orders that we have from the Ministry of Defence of the Republika Srpska, in this particular case Zvornik Secretariat, which references the general mobilisation of buses from all over Eastern Bosnia. Those buses which will subsequently be used for the movement of the Bosnian Muslim people out of Potocari and will also be used subsequently for the movement of prisoners. This order went out on the morning of 12 July. It references a Main Staff order regarding the mobilisation of buses and you can see effectively the process by which the Ministry of Defence is requisitioning civilian buses and directing that they are sent to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have the Main Staff army order that's references here, do you know?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I do not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is this -- you mentioned a series. Is this one, are there others like it or related to it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are -- on 12 July, there are two additional ones, two other areas. And on 13 July, there are three more mobilisation orders for additional buses and transportation assets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've just chosen this one as a representative example?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, 12 July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's the next document, I believe 427.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a Drina Corps order also with respect to the provision of buses to all of its subordinate formations. While the Ministry of Defence was mobilising buses within the civil community, within the military structure of the Drina Corps, the Drina Corps commander was directing that all the units listed here mobilise their buses that are under military control and again send them to Bratunac. It's noted that this order goes to the commands of the 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade, the 1st Birac Infantry Brigade, the 2nd Romanija Motorised Brigade, the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, the 1st and 5th Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade and the 1st Milici Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Should the commander of the Bratunac Brigade at this time know about this order and this process of requisitioning buses to be used for the transportation as stated?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given that this order is sent by the commander of the Drina Corps, this is something that the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade commander should have been aware of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On 12 July, do you have any documents or intercepts to indicate the location of Vidoje Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I do not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Does this actually make any reference to the Bratunac Brigade providing any buses?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it does in the second paragraph, where it notes that the buses that are provided by the Zvornik Infantry Brigades and the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade shall be filled up at their own commands, which means the units responsible have to make sure that they have appropriate fuel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what part of the Bratunac Brigade would be involved in the fuel?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would normally fall under the province of the assistant commander for rear services, Major Trisic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's go to the next document in the narrative which should be original number and proper number P180, if we will ignore what is marked on this exhibit. We will have that corrected.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an intercept on 12 July 1995 which reflects one of the issues that I went into in detail in my narrative, which was the involvement of the Drina Corps in the actual process of assembling the buses and controlling the movement of those buses, making sure they are showing up in the appropriate place at the appropriate time. In this particular intercept, an individual called Krstic and an individual as Lieutenant Colonel Krsmanovic. Now, Lieutenant Colonel Krsmanovic is identified as the transportation services officer of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And according to this intercept, these buses are supposed to report at 1700 at the Bratunac stadium?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would the Bratunac Brigade normally be involved in any of this process that Krstic and Krsmanovic appear to be involved in from this intercept?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, certainly as indicated by Krstic in this case, Bratunac is sending buses. And given the location and physical proximity of the Bratunac Brigade to the Bratunac stadium, it would have been logical for the assistant commander of rear services to be greatly assisting the transportation services chief of the Drina Corps in facilitating this process. Logically they have the best knowledge of the situation in and around Bratunac with respect to all of the requirements necessary to accomplish this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next exhibit which should be properly marked as 184. Again, let's ignore the marking in the right corner. And just briefly, what is this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a synopsis of a 12 July conversation which reflects, again, Lieutenant Colonel Krsmanovic, some subscriber, we're not sure who, informing him that they only have two buses available and that they have no fuel for these buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next one. It should be conversation at 1200 hours on the 12th. It should be P186. Again, ignoring the right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a conversation again discussing the process of collecting buses from all over Eastern Bosnia. The individual listed there, Rado Kovac, it is my understanding that he an individual associated with the logistics organs of the Main Staff. And it notes the fact that they're sending empty tanker trucks and also the request had been forwarded for fuel to Krstic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next one, P188, a conversation at 1210 hours or a brief reference, I should say.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again in this brief reference, a conversation noted between Krstic and Krsmanovic. And this is the first indication that rather than beginning the movement of the population from Potocari on 12 July at 1700 or from the marshalling at the Bratunac stadium, that apparently the plan has changed and they want to begin the movement immediately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, we hear the name Krstic. Who do you think this is?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is General Major Krstic who at this time is still the chief of staff of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And let's go to another conversation on the 12th, P189. It does not have a time on it in the exhibit that we have.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular exhibit, it's just the continuing process that a member -- the most logical member, in fact, of the Drina Corps staff is involved in continuing to try to assemble transportation assets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next exhibit, P190, another intercept, 1220. This time it appears to be labelled as a CSB or MUP intercept.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it about this that you find significant in the narrative?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again as alluded to in the narrative, and as I've testified prior, one of the most significant resources in the VRS at the time or lack of resources is the issue of fuel. With the embargo from Serbia in place and fuel was a highly rationed and valuable resource, which units there had to ration and report on daily. What they're doing here is this is a conversation referencing an individual Miletic who, I believe, is Major General Miletic of the Main Staff, chief of operations. And they're talking about the acquiring of over 200 tons of fuel and in this case they're not sure whether it's 200 litres or 200 tons, but the movement of fuel with respect to the trucks and buses that are still leaving for these areas and heading towards Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have described General Miletic as chief of operations. On July 12th, what position do you think he was filling?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I've discussed previously, on July 12th due to the absence of General Milovanovic, General Major Miletic was also performing the function of the acting chief of staff of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Going on to the next exhibit, P434.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, again discussing the issue of fuel where the command of the Drina Corps is requesting fuel from the Main Staff officially, 10.000 litres of diesel, 2.000 of petrol. And essentially General Zivanovic is saying as soon as the fuel is made available, we'll pick up -- we'll make arrangements to have it picked up. The other interesting note in this particular instance is second-to-last line of the paragraph starting on 12 July where it notes that, at least in this respect, the final destination of the buses is not known.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell whether that's the final destination towards where it's going to pick people up versus whether or not it's final destination towards where it was going to let them off? Can you tell that regarding what the final destination might be?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given -- in context with the earlier Drina Corps order which talks about buses going to the Bratunac stadium, I read this in context then to be that the final destination of where the buses will go after Bratunac is yet to be determined.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And we still have General Zivanovic signing as commander of the corps. Is that right? Or is that a "za" underneath that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the original B/C/S version, no, sir, that is General Zivanovic's signature to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Exhibit 435, what is this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document -- this is the English language translation of a handwritten document that was found in the security office of the Bratunac Brigade during the OTP search. What this document indicates is a list compiled 12 July, 2100 hours, and it contains lists of bus companies and licence plates and how much fuel was put in the buses on those days. It indicates that in most cases the fuel, in fact, for the buses was provided in Bratunac and not at other locations. And it totals up to 3.415 litres according to their calculations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: And this is the B/C/S version of that list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any information on who actually compiled this list?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I do not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Going back in time to another intercept at 1240 hours, it should be P191, what do you want to point out here?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This particular intercept between one subscriber, X, and it is identified as Panorama. And Panorama is the telephonic code word for the Main Staff, notes the fact that the evacuation is starting for those who want to go towards Kladanj. And then later down subscriber Y, who we don't know who it is, notes the fact that buses, trucks should be sent, a water tanker should be sent to give them food and water. It's all been organised here, and this subscriber reflects the fact that, "I talked with them and will accept all the civilians who want to and they can stay and those who don't want to can chose to go where they want to go." So in this context, subscriber Y believes that the individuals who are going want to go and that the individuals who want to remain can, in fact, do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And how does that intercept relate to the charges of forcible transfer in this case?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, clearly in that context, subscriber Y is indicating that to his knowledge, people will have a choice whether they want to be evacuated or whether they want to remain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next intercept. It should be P192. And this is 1250 hours. Ten minutes later -- I believe 10 minutes. Yes. And the last exhibit.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an intercept where the people are identified as General Mladic and an unidentified male person where the issue is again being discussed. In one respect it says here, attributed to General Mladic, monitor the situation, don't let small groups of them sneak in. He notes they've all capitulated and surrendered and will evacuate them all, those who want to and those who don't want to. X reflects, "I understand, General." Mladic is cautioning, "Don't issue any statements and don't interrupt them over the radio station. We'll open a corridor towards Kladanj." And in the last line attributed to General Mladic, making it clear, let them pass there, take a patrol out and make sure that the mines and obstacles are removed from the road that connects the area that we know as the tunnel, the Luke school area, with Kladanj, which is Bosnian Muslim territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So one of the previous exhibits where Zivanovic in an order notes, I believe around 10.00, did not know where the final destination is, does this seem to solve that issue?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that level it does, and again at another level it highlights one of the issues that one has to be aware of when using intercept information, and when judging the reliability thereof.
