While it is entirely possible that the information that is collected is accurate and reliable, ultimately there is no way to know except in the context of analysis whether or not the two subscribers know what they're talking about. So in this respect, while the last intercept is an accurate and valid description of the conversation, subscriber Y had a different understanding of events as reflected than the subscribers in this conversation. So when we talk about the issue of reliability, it's reliability of process, and it's also reliability of information contextually compared to events occurring on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next one which should be properly marked as P193. Can you tell us about this intercept.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an intercept from 12 July 1995, dated -- at 1305 hours. Initially the subscribers were identified as Krstic and Sobot. Now, Major Sobot is identified on the chart as a member of the technical services staff of the Drina Corps. It also discusses or alludes to the fact that Krsmanovic set off towards Krstic 15 minutes ago. It discusses at the first part the number of buses that are moving. And about one-third the way through the conversation you could hear through the switchboard being put through to the Vlasenica Brigade and General Krstic asking for, in this case, Major Kosoric, who is a different individual from Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric, his intelligence chief. In this case, Major Kosoric is the commander of the Vlasenica Brigade. He is put through to an individual named Savo whom we understand to be the deputy commander of the Vlasenica Light Infantry Brigade, where General Krstic instructs him to get out to the location towards the tunnel and he uses the -- he talks around the issue, 12 kilometres towards Drava. Drava is the telephonic code name of the Birac Infantry Brigade. So putting this on context on the ground, we know which tunnel that they're talking about --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, do you have that map.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I can't recall if that map actually has -- goes as far as Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't believe I have the map, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could maybe just take a moment and get the big map out, it might be easier to see also. Anyway as we're getting the bigger map, you can just -- well, let's just set it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honours can see that okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Butler, can you help us describe the areas that you think are being talked about in this. Don't get too far from the mike.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular instance, the areas that we're talking about are from Bratunac, the road to the intersection Konjevic Polje, towards Milici, through Vlasenica. The area of Tisca. The small village of Luke. And from here, the Bosnian Muslims walked through this tunnel and past to the city or town of Kladanj on the Federation side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So where it says, "From where you are 12 kilometres towards Drava," what does that mean, "From where you are"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the zone of the Birac Light Infantry Brigade -- or Birac Infantry Brigade, Drava, "From where you are," Vlasenica, 12 kilometres up is approximately the Tisca area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So for the record, Mr. Butler has described the area of the Drava Brigade being a few kilometres north of Tisca. And where is this tunnel, again, Mr. Butler, just to make it clear?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the tunnel is located just at the boarder between -- or the line of contact at that time between the Federation and the Republika Srpska at the village of Luke.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And it says -- Krstic says: "That's where they will be disembarking," and who do you think he's referring to?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that context, he is referring to the Bosnian Muslim women and children and elderly who are being moved out of Potocari on 12 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he goes on to say: "Take care. Nothing must happen to any of them." How does that fit into your knowledge of the overall situation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, with respect to the overall situation, the Bosnian Muslim women and children who were moving down as part of -- or who were being transported out of the former enclave and from Potocari, were generally not abused and were safeguarded through the process of putting them on the bus and moving them out, dropping them off at the Luke village area, and allowing them to continue on. There are only a very few isolated instances where any individuals who were women and children on those buses were subject to any form of abuse. At the same time, particularly in the early series of buses, we've been able to establish that some Bosnian Muslim men were put on those buses or were able to sneak on. And when those buses were emptied at the village of Luke, any Bosnian Muslim men who were deemed to be of military age were separated out at that time and were subsequently held in an area which we call the school at Luke. Subsequently, as indicated in the Krstic record and in evidence that I believe is before this Trial Chamber, those individuals were taken out and executed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did this separation at Luke first begin happening, according to the information you have?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It started occurring on the afternoon of 12 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that information comes from Major Boering who has testified in this case?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir. Major Boering, of course, being the first UN officer or accompanying those first UN convoys.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record this large map Mr. Butler has referred to is 16.1. All right. What is the next document that you wish to refer to in the narrative of this 12 July time frame?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll move to my next binder. This is a document that was seized by the OTP during a search of the Zvornik CSB centre, centre for public security. And what it discusses is the report of the chief of the CSB, Dragomir Vasic. And it discusses his recounting or his reporting of the events as they occur in the beginning -- on the morning of 12 July. It notes that paragraph 12, that there was a meeting with General Mladic and General Krstic which was held at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters at 0800 hours, and it is readable on the B/C/S version at that time, at which tasks were assigned to all those involved. Paragraph 3 reflects that the military operation is continuing according to plan. And it reflects that the Bosnian Muslim military is fleeing towards the villages of Suceska while the civilians have gathered at Potocari. And again in that respect, if I can with the larger map, highlight the one thing that was occurring, that village complex that was described is located in this area here, which is the Bardera triangle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the area of Suceska village?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Suceska village. And in fact, in Susnjari and Jaglici is where the column was forming, indicating that by their 8.00 in the morning meeting, that certainly General Mladic, General Krstic and the military leadership had not put the pieces of information yet together that were being reported to bring them to the conclusion that, in fact, the 28th Division was not where they thought it was, but was assembling in the Susnjari and Jaglici area. It also notes in paragraph 4 some of the more routine police-related issues with respect to putting together civil authority for the now-occupied town of Srebrenica. Paragraph 5 reflects that there will be a meeting at 1000 hours and that agreement will be reached on the evacuation of the civilian population from Potocari to Kladanj. So certainly in the case of Dragomir Vasic, he understood walking away from that 8.00 meeting in the morning that that was what the conclusion of the 10.00 meeting was going to be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do we see Mr. Vasic at the 10.00 Hotel Fontana meeting?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. He is videotaped as present. It also notes in paragraph 6, joint police forces are advancing on Potocari with the aim of taking the UNPROFOR personnel prisoner, surrounding the entire population, and cleansing the area of enemy troops. And paragraph 7, the main military objectives are to ensure that all roads leading from Srebrenica to Skelani, Bratunac, and Vlasenica are passable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, going back to paragraph 6, based on your knowledge, do you find that statement to be credible?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do. We have information that indicates that, again based off of the 10 July order by Acting Minister Kovac for the special police brigade and the company from CSB Zvornik -- sorry, the company from PJP, the first PJP company from Zvornik, those are, in fact, joint police forces. They assemble in Bratunac. They spend the evening of 11 July outside of the enclave near the Zuti Most checkpoint area and then on the 12 of July they are instructed to start walking towards Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Surrounding the entire civilian population, did that happen?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, a large number of the special police units did get to Potocari, and as the Court understands, they are seen on videotape there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there other troops as well?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about this statement, "Cleansing the area of enemy troops." What do you make of this term "cleansing," in this context?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this context, the phrase "cleansing" does not have the same legal connotation that is frequently used here. What we are talking about in this respect is something more related to sweeping a particular area. The military objective to be that after a particular unit passes through that area, there will be no more enemy forces behind them. So by cleansing that area or by sweeping through that area, it is in effect a military operation to secure that area and make sure there are no remaining military forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't see any ethnic connotation to this comment?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on paragraph 7, is that correct, that on 12 July at about the time this was written that the objective of the military operations was the main objective -- that's a question mark. It may have been a problem in being able to view it.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly with respect to as an objective, keeping the routes of communication open is a normal military objective, and given the context that they know they are going to be moving the civilian population out of Potocari, the communication route from Bratunac through Vlasenica, which is the road we've previously discussed, paramount to keeping that open.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the other main objectives that day. I think you've discussed some, but if you can just briefly remind us of the military objectives as you were aware of them.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again as discussed in paragraph 3, it notes the military objective at that time is sweeping through the Bardera triangle where the army believed that the bulk of the 28th Infantry Division was still located.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So if you could go to the next exhibit. I believe it is 440.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order from the command of the Drina Corps directed to the commands of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade and the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. And it specifies two tasks. Paragraph 1 directs that the command of the 1st Zvornik Brigade will assign a motorised patrol of military traffic police to regulate the traffic at the Konjevic Polje junction, reflecting that the priority shall be given to buses travelling from Srebrenica and that the military police should take over control of the intersection or junction at 1630 hours on 12 July 1995. The second one is directed to the command of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, and it says: Will, in cooperation with the Bratunac SJB, public security station, regulate the traffic in both ways on the Konjevic Polje/Bratunac road, and particularly around the stadium in the town of Bratunac. Again, priority will be given to the buses for the evacuation. The last line, be ready at 1630 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I note this talks about in cooperation, the Bratunac Brigade will in cooperation. Is this used in anything similar to the context of the word "cooperation" as you had previously referred to in the JNA regs?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular context, I believe what it means is the Bratunac Brigade is being instructed to find and coordinate -- that's my word not theirs, find and deal with the Bratunac SJB and deal with the issues related to securing the route. That particular instance, it's not an order directing the Bratunac Brigade to take command of the traffic security service of the Bratunac SJB, but it gives the Bratunac Brigade the primary rather role in ensuring that these events occur.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we tell from this order who is in overall command of the units mentioned in paragraph 2?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In effect, it is General Major Milenko Zivanovic, the commander of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any indications whether or not the Bratunac Brigade followed this order?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly by, as the intercepts indicate, the evacuation of the Bosnian Muslims started taking place approximately noon. We know from the context of other information that's become available and is before the Court that Bratunac Brigade military police were active in Potocari as well as active in escorting bus convoys. Bratunac civilian police were also doing that. Certainly both the police and the military were in position to regulate traffic along the Bratunac/Konjevic Polje road, so in that respect it appears that the order as to securing the routes of transportation and facilitating the movement out was, in fact, carried out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What's the next document you wanted to discuss? I believe it's Exhibit 441.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the daily combat report of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. It says St. Peter's Day. It is 12 July 1995. And it reflects on 12 July 1995 what is occurring in the zone of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remind us what time normally these things were supposed to be done, and if you can, tell us if there's any way to actually get a better -- better identify the actual time this was written.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we look at the B/C/S teletype version of this report, while we cannot identify the time the report was drafted or typed, we have on the B/C/S version the initials of the communications clerk as to when it was sent and as to what day it was sent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 1630 hours.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what can you -- what's the significance of this document?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Going back to the English language translation, that paragraph 7 indicates that the command is aware of the transport of the Bosnian Muslim population from -- in Potocari, that it's underway, and that their number is 10.000 refugees are expecting to be transported. It also notes with respect to the enemy situation in paragraph 1, that they're aware that during the day the enemy tried to break through or withdraw from the former enclave along the Milacevici/Jaglici/Bokcin Potok direction towards Tuzla. So by the afternoon of 12 July, it is now becoming clear within the decision-making organs, the brigade, the Drina Corps headquarters, and even the Main Staff, that in fact the bulk of the Bosnian Muslim military forces are now trying to make their way from the Susnjari/Jaglica area to Federation lines at Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We see that in this Bratunac Brigade report. How can you say that about the Drina Corps and the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we go on to further documents, we will see their own reflections of reporting where they gain the awareness and where they're reporting the situation as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this daily combat report is sent where?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is sent to the command of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does the Drina Corps send on their own report?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. They send a daily report to the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we'll be going over some of those reports shortly, I take it.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next document you've got. I believe that's 442, and what is this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it is. This is a document that was discovered during the OTP search of the Bratunac Brigade headquarters in the office of the security officer. This is a listing of -- I want to make sure I get the number right, 387 individuals who are suspected of being individuals who committed war crimes in the general area of the listed municipalities and are believed to be in Srebrenica. If you go to -- and I'm sorry the pages aren't numbered, but at the last page of the English language translation, the final notation indicates that this list was compiled on 12 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what significance do you give this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, looking at the historical context of the area, over the past three years, particularly late 1992, early 1993 time period, during the rather intense fighting there, there were a lot of incidents that occurred which the Bosnian Muslim -- I'm sorry the Bosnian Serbs considered to be war crimes perpetrated against them by Bosnian Muslim forces. As part of their own laws and internal reporting requirements, lists were being kept of individuals, presumably that one day when they had access to those individuals, criminal charges could be filed against them. And this list obviously represents their roll-up names of individuals that they believe are among those people in and around the Potocari area or who were from Srebrenica as of 12 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On 12, 13, and 14 July when we know there are literally thousands of Muslim prisoners in the Bratunac area, do you see in your analysis any effort to identify the individuals on this list through any normal means?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we've -- this Court has seen evidence that there was wholesale destruction of Muslim property, including identification documents. Would identification documents be important in identifying people amongst the Muslim prisoners that matched the identity of these potential war criminals?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: While it can't be denied that many of the members of the Bratunac Brigade and other individuals in that area would recognise these people by sight as they were their former neighbours, certainly the issue of the wholesale destruction of identification documents would run counter to the listed goal here of identifying these people for criminal prosecution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next document. I believe it's 443. What is this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document from the command of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade to the Drina Corps command, attention Major Golic. Major Golic, as indicated, is an intelligence officer with the command of the Drina Corps. And during this period, he is in Vlasenica. What this document indicates is a small bit of intelligence information that is known to an individual called Captain Pecanac concerning what they believe are the intentions of the Bosnian Muslim column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So do you know who Captain Pecanac is?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Captain Pecanac is an individual identified as an officer of the Main Staff security organ, and is somebody who is closely identified as being responsible for the personal security of General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell from this document where it was sent from?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you look at the B/C/S version, it clearly indicates that it was sent from the command of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. And as we'll become very familiar, the signature of the code clerk of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. So while the document in question was drafted by an officer of the Main Staff, it was sent through the communications of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell from this document whether it would have been made secret, like "for eyes only," of intel security like we've seen in these counter-intelligence reports?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. It's just specifically directed to an intelligence officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the information in it about prisoners, does that have anything to do with counter-intelligence from what you see or could it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I could take you back briefly, I apologise, to Exhibit 441. It was the St. Peter's Day, 12 July, daily combat report. This is under the name of Vidoje Blagojevic. Can you make anything -- do you have a handwritten version of that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I notice it's cut off in the bottom, but can you make any analysis regarding whether or not Mr. Blagojevic signed this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular respect, I recognise this signature as being that of Major Eskic, who is the chief of personnel. There is another partial signature, but because of the cut off, I could not tell you who that could be. I suspect we have the original in the evidence vault.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the one that's cut off look anything like the signature that you've become familiar with with Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would hate to speculate on that just based on the copy. We do have the original handwritten version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll take a better look at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just a minor point. I take it at some point the gentleman will be qualified as a handwriting analyst as well? Because he's testifying now to identifying signatures and I was unaware -- I know he's an analyst, but now we're getting into a whole separate area of expertise, handwriting analysis. So I take it, if he's not an analyst, he's just giving his opinion based on his comparison and not necessarily an expert opinion as to the signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: That's what I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. As Mr. Butler said that simply yesterday. We're not holding him out as an expert in that field. He's just saying it looks like the one he's been looking at. I don't think we should take -- we should take it for whatever value the Court wants to give it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What's the next document you have? And that is 444, I believe.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a 12 July document from the command of the Drina Corps intelligence department to the VRS Main Staff intelligence sector and also to the Drina Corps Bratunac IKM, listed as forward command post, personally for Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric. And what this is is this is an intelligence report which indicates that at 1300 hours on 12 July, an enemy soldier was captured and they've extracted combat information from that soldier, which discusses the future intentions of the column. It also reflects the fact in the last paragraph that the Drina Corps duty officer Lieutenant Colonel Jovicic and an operations officer Lieutenant Colonel Ognjenovic are aware of this information. It also notes that the intelligence organ presented the information to the chief of the Vlasenica MUP so that MUP members could be sent to the generally area of Konjevic Polje. And it's also indicated that the command of the Milici Light Infantry Brigade has also been informed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this something that the command staff of the Bratunac Brigade should be aware of?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given that it's going to the Bratunac IKM and that it is reflective strictly of intelligence related to the column as something that would impact their area, this is information that they should be aware of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this says the Drina Corps Bratunac forward command post or IKM. We've already heard about and seen documents related to the Pribicevac forward command post. Are they related, these two places?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are both considered forward command posts. The Pribicevac command post on 12 July is still controlling military sweep operations in the Bardera triangle. The Bratunac IKM or the Drina Corps forward command post at Bratunac is now controlling operations with respect to the evacuation or the movement of the Bosnian Muslim column -- or Bosnian Muslim population from Potocari as well as now the growing conflict with the Bosnian Muslim column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What can you tell us about the forward command post at Pribicevac? How long was it up and operating as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our information indicates that by approximately 1800 hours on 12 July 1995, the forward command post at Pribicevac was shut down and that the personnel were moved to the headquarters at Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: 3 (redacted) . However, we have a number of documents that were received by the IKM command post at Pribicevac throughout the day of the 12th July until approximately 1800. That's why it is my assessment that that command post, in fact, discontinued its operation by 1800 hours on 12 July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can -- the fact that this is directed to Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric, does this give us any indication where he may be at the time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does indicate that Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric is in or around the Bratunac Brigade headquarters or at least close enough to where this information can be made available to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any significant military reason that you know of for people of high rank to be still at Pribicevac at about the time of this, 420 hours on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given what we know of the greater context, the only high-ranking Drina Corps officer at the Pribicevac command post during the afternoon of 12 July 1995 is Colonel Ognjenovic, the operations officer, and several staff involved in communications. Most of the general officers, including General Krstic were in and around the Bratunac area in about this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I think it's break time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, we have been able to provide you with the original B/C/S of Exhibit 441. Counsel have had a chance to see that and you've had a chance to see it. Could you point out to us in the left corner what you can make of the signature block and the information before that.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to the signature, I do not recognise the signature. I would note that, as indicated, there's the "za" there indicating that this individual has signed for the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. If we could go on to your next command exhibit for 12 July, I believe it's 445. And could you tell us what this is and what you want to talk about.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a Drina Corps command intelligence section document dated 12 July 1995. It was directed to the Main Staff intelligence sector. It's directed to the Drina Corps IKM in Pribicevac, General Krstic. It is directed to the Drina Corps IKM Bratunac Lieutenant Colonel Popovic. And the chiefs of the intelligence organs of the relevant brigades, in this particular case the Milici Light Infantry Brigade, the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, the Vlasenica Light Infantry Brigade, the 2nd Romanija Motorised Brigade, the Birac Infantry Brigade, the Zvornik Infantry Brigade. It's also directed to the MUP in Vlasenica, Milici, and Zvornik for their information. The last addressee is the MUP of Republika Srpska and also the RDB state security department of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who's it authored by?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This particular document is authored by General Major Zdravko Tolimir, who we know is the assistant commander for intelligence and security if the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is he sending it from, by this document?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based off of the header information, it's my assessment that he's sending this document from the Drina Corps headquarters in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what in the substance of the document do you want to point out?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is again a series of intelligence reports based on information obtained from individuals who are surrendering or being captured from the column. And in this particular place, it indicates -- in this particular document, it indicates the prisoner was taken at about 1800 hours on 12 July in the sector of the village of Kajici on the Bratunac/Pribicevac road. That particular location corresponds to the location of the 4th Infantry Battalion of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. It reflects, again, not only the prisoner of war's name, but information that he has which will be of value to commanders who are dealing with the column. In paragraph -- the second paragraph of the second page, it reflects the note that: "We have informed the organs of the MUP of RS in Konjevic Polje about the illegal corridor use by the Muslims of the Srebrenica, since it is their task to control the Bratunac/Konjevic Polje road." So in this particular instance, it is the Drina Corps acknowledging that they understand that the task of the MUP in this particular instance is to control that road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How can it be Drina Corps if it's coming from a Main Staff general?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, as I've indicated, because the actual document originating from the headquarters of the Drina Corps, it is from the Drina Corps. We believe, or certainly I believe, that at this point in time, General Tolimir is at the headquarters in Vlasenica and he directs this report to the sent out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It also notes that the commands of the Bratunac, Zvornik, and Milici Brigades, in cooperation with the SJBs and their areas of responsibility shall regulate traffic during the night along the Bratunac/Milici/Vlasenica and Zvornik/Kojevic Polje/Vlasenica roads. They shall only allow passage that VRS and MUP vehicles and units on an official or combat mission around the former enclave of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I may have missed this, but I want to ask you specifically about this comment in the third -- it looks like the second large paragraph the way its been typed up where it says: "Intelligence organs shall propose measures to be taken by commands to prevent armed Muslims from illegally reaching Tuzla and Kladanj, such as setting up ambushes along the routes they use in order to arrest them and prevent possible surprises against civilians and/or combat units along those routes." Now, first of all is intelligence organs -- is that correct in this -- a correct translation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the B/C/S version, right here you see after "za," you see the letters "OBP." OBP is the acronym for intelligence and security, as opposed to straight intelligence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So what I want to ask you about is if intelligence and security organs shall propose measures to be taken by commands to prevent armed Muslims from illegally reaching Tuzla, how does that fit into the definitions and the job duties of the intelligence and security organs that you've discussed previously?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it reflects a very good example of how the intelligence and security organs, given the information that is flowing through them with respect to enemy prisoners of war, using that information to provide the best possible advice to their commanders, as to where forces should be deployed, where collection points should be set up, what procedures should be taken, and again, that's the classical responsibility of the staff officer, to make recommendations for the best possible uses of the available assets to the commander for his decision. So in this respect, I see this as a traditional application of the command and staff process.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Unless there is something else in this document, let's go on to the next one. Exhibit 446.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is a report from the chief of the Zvornik CSB, Dragomir Vasic, to his superiors in the Republika Srpska MUP. And it discusses the situation from his perspective on 12 July 1995, noting to his superiors that the evacuation and transport of the civilian population is underway. It notes that intelligence information that they're receiving about 300 men led by Zulfo Tursunovic and Dudic. It reflects their knowledge that the Zvornik Infantry Brigade has been tasked at blocking them on the hill feature Crni Vrh. In addition to other intelligence information, it lays out the locations of the MUP units along the road, reflecting that the Sekovici special detachment, the 1st company of the PJP from Zvornik CJB, and the 5th company of the Zvornik CJB are blocking that particular section of road with a goal of destroying these forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that consistent with other documents that we've talked about?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it is. As we've discussed previously, part of the problem was that through the gap in the lines between the Milici Brigade and the Bratunac Brigade, this is where this column was going. And again, as a function of terrain, the path of that column comes extremely close to the road between Bratunac and Konjevic Polje, and perhaps it would be better to show you on the map. The path comes very close to the road here, and then ultimately crosses the road around the Cerska River and then continues up. So in order to fill that gap and place forces there, the most readily available forces were those of the MUP and, in fact, they were deployed along that road from roughly the village of Sandici to Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you find any of the information in this short report incorrect?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. It actually appears to be a pretty accurate picture of the column at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next document. This should be 447.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is another command of the Drina Corps intelligence report for 12 July 1995. And the last of the series that we have from the Drina Corps with this respect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Authored by who?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular instance, if I can go quickly to page 2 -- well, I'm not sure who it is authored by. It is, in fact, released under the signature of General Major Zdravko Tolimir again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What can you say about the time it went out or was received?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you can tell from this particular translation -- well, you can't tell which time it was sent, you have a series of received stamps. This particular one, if I can scroll down, reflects the stamp of the intelligence communication centre where they received it, indicating that it was received by them approximately at 2200 hours, 12 July 1995. Moving further up, you have a stamp from the operations centre of the 2nd Romanija Brigade, reflecting when they're logging it in for their own administrative processes. Just to show you what that looks like in the original. This is the text with the communications centre stamp, and this is the stamp from the 2nd Romanija Brigade operations people, as they assigned it a number for tracking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what in particular about this document would you point out to us?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular case, it is again sent to the intelligence and security departments. It's also sent to the command of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps and the Bosnia Corps. It is sent to the Pribicevac IKM and it is sent to the Bratunac IKM. And at this time despite the fact that it's being sent there, that communications centre shut down approximately 1800. So we have no evidence to suggest that it was ever received there. It's also noted going directly to individuals General Krstic and Lieutenant Colonel Popovic. It's further addressed to the intelligence and security OBP organs of -- again a number of units, the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, the Milici Light Infantry Brigade --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We don't need to. We can see those.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. This particular report discusses intelligence information which the VRS is learning by monitoring the radio network of elements of the 28th Muslim Division. And again, from this and prisoner of war intelligence-related information, they're putting out the intelligence picture as to what the intent of the column is. The last paragraph on the first page, again noting that the OBP organs of the brigade commands will propose to the commanders of the units along the line of withdrawal of elements what measures to undertake -- or actually to undertake measures to prevent the withdrawal and to capture enemy soldiers. Going to the second page, the first paragraph reflects that special attention should be paid to monitoring the gaps in our forward defence line and possible escape routes along the illegal corridors, as well as to possible sudden attacks on residential areas, rear areas of combat formations and defence elements. As the last issue, last paragraph, the OBP organs will brief the MUP organs in their respective zones or area of responsibility on the information received. They will draw up joint plans for breaking up and liquidating the enemy formations trying to escape from the Srebrenica enclave towards Tuzla and Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As part of the traditional role of the security organ in the regulations, they are a coordinating interface, if you will, between the military security organ and the civil police organ. So they are the people who are charged to coordinate this type of activity with the civilian police to ensure that everything is operating as it should be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to take you to the paragraph immediately above the command of the Romanija Motorised brigade that says: "Although it is very important to arrest as many members of the shattered Muslim units as possible or liquidate them if they resist, it is equally important to note down the names of all men fit for military service who are being evacuated from the UNPROFOR base in Potocari." Now, this is sent out late on the 12th of July. Do you have any indications that this was being done?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about those names we saw out of the Bratunac Brigade dated 12 July?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were a list of names of people who were to be screened. Those are not, to my knowledge, a list of names of individuals who had been collected. They certainly don't qualify as individuals fit for military service who are being evacuated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, Mr. Blagojevic is raising his hand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes, Mr. Blagojevic. THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would just like to say one sentence. I can take a lot of things, and I'm a very tolerant person, but when it is said here that this list is a list of the Bratunac Brigade, that I cannot stand. They should say where this is stated, and this is an opportunity to do so. Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you Mr. Blagojevic. I believe that this Trial Chamber has given you the instructions. If you have any problems, please write down on a piece of paper and send it to your counsel. But anyway, since this issue is raised by Mr. Blagojevic, Mr. McCloskey, would you please ask some questions to this witness to make it clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, perhaps you could find that list and we can discuss it again briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Exhibit 435, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ma'am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: No, that's not the list you're looking for.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, if you could just show us what it says at the top of that list. List of war criminals -- and also if you could put the B/C/S top of the list so Mr. Blagojevic can see it. Put the English and the B/C/S maybe next to each other so we can both read the top of the lists.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "List of war criminals known to the command of the 1st Light Infantry Brigade, who committed war crimes in the area of Bratunac, Srebrenica, Milici, Vlasenica, and Skelani municipalities and are believed to be in Srebrenica." So given that heading, would it make sense that this is a list following the order of General Tolimir to make a list of the able-bodied men from Potocari?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now it says "The 1st Light Infantry Brigade." That's the English. Does it tell us in the B/C/S which one that is?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. It just says 1.LPBR.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many light infantry brigades were in that area of units listed, Vlasenica, Milici?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Bratunac Brigade had a light infantry brigade. The Milici municipality had a light infantry brigade. The Vlasenica municipality had a light infantry brigade. Skelani had a separate battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can we go to the end of the document in English.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: And this is the English version -- this is -- both versions say the same thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's Bratunac, 12 July 1995. Now, where and when was this document found by the OTP?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was found -- I can't tell you the exact date of the search. It was, I believe, in January or February 1998. The document was found at the headquarters of the former Bratunac Brigade and specifically in the office of the security officer of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. That's all I have on that area. So, Mr. Butler, if we could go back to where we were. Do you recall where that was? I think we were just finishing up that document, which I believe was 447. And if you don't have anymore to say about that, we can go on to the next, 448. What is this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is another report from the RS RDB state security on 12 July 1995, again reflecting the situation as they're reporting it in the greater Bratunac area, and now extending towards the greater Zvornik area. It indicates that their knowledge is being confirmed that large groups of Muslims left the area on the night between 11 and 12 July, who's leading the group, what their intentions are. It reflects that a third group was set off at 1600 hours on 12 July and was ambushed near the village of Sandici and that four Muslim soldiers were captured. It discusses information from them. It reflects the fact that to their knowledge, that they're aware of the knowledge that traffic has been suspended on the Zvornik/Konjevic Polje/Han Pijesak road and the Zvornik/Caparde/Sekovici and Vlasenica road. It notes the agreements reach to evacuate the civilians from of Potocari and that approximately 8500 people were transported out. It also reflects the fact that the transportation or evacuation was suspended at night and will resume on the morning 13th of July. An indication, in this case, when this report was drafted. The final sentence reflects that it is the knowledge of the state security people there that among the people staying in Potocari, there are hardly any men fit for fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not the final sentence in the document, but is that the final sentence related to the Srebrenica area?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to the Bratunac area, that is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next document. Now, we're going in the chronology, and I believe the next document is the -- a document the Court is familiar with from previous exhibits, 449, the Bratunac Brigade military police log. If you could just go to 12 July. All right. Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you use it in your analysis?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And -- it seems to me we've discussed this already, but perhaps I'm mistaken. If you could just briefly point out the important parts of this.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This documents reflects the activities of the Bratunac Brigade military police during the day and evening and through the following morning of 13 July 1995. It reflects that the police were engaged in securing UNHCR, which is what we all have become familiar with understanding as the UNPROFOR, and the surrender of the Muslim people from Srebrenica in Zuti Most to the Serb soldiers in Bratunac. One part of the police force has been secured sick and wounded in the clinic, and in that respect, as I believe, testimony has been led about a number of individuals, Bosnian Muslims, who were transported from the UN medical centre in Potocari to the Bratunac clinic. And it discusses the passage of trucks transporting refugees from the Srebrenica enclave through Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you think this means that "Muslim people from Srebrenica in Zuti Most to the Serb soldiers in Bratunac." Zuti Most, where is Zuti Most in relation to Potocari where all the civilians are known to have been then?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may refer to the map. Where the United Nations forces established Checkpoint Papa, just on the other side there was a VRS Bratunac military police checkpoint at a location known as Zuti Most or Yellow Bridge. So in that context, Yellow Bridge is just on the north -- slightly north-eastern side of the enclave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any information that Muslims specifically surrendered at Zuti Most?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I do not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what that might be a reference to?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may infer to the fact that military police going from Zuti Most proceeded into Potocari. And of course, I believe the Court has seen evidence of Bratunac Brigade military police in Potocari on 12 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then there's a mention of sick and wounded. Now, this Trial Chamber has heard evidence of sick and wounded Muslims being tended to at the UN base and I believe in the Bratunac health centre. And eventually these folks were shipped out. Has the investigation revealed whether or not there was ever any separation or abuse of the Muslims known as the sick and wounded?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. To my knowledge, again summarising the investigation, all of the individuals referred to the sick and wounded who were individuals turned over by the UN and placed in the Bratunac military health centre under the supervision of the VRS and the UN, were eventually released and repatriated either through the ICRC or at the end of the war. Only in one instance was an individual who was suspected of being a war criminal separated from that group of individuals and taken into custody by authorities from CSB Zvornik and he, too, did survive the war. So for that collection of individuals, there's no evidence of any wrongdoing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And I think the rest of this speaks or itself, so let's go on to the next exhibit. We may come back to that police log as we go through the chronology, the military police log. So what do you have as your next exhibit for the 12th of July narrative?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the daily combat report from the Zvornik Infantry Brigade to the command of the Drina Corps. Where I believe the value of this document is is related to Prosecution Exhibit 440, because in this document it discusses, based on that document, it reaffirms the fact that one military police attachment was sent to Konjevic Polje pursuant to your order, and it also reflects the fact that the Zvornik Brigade sent to Bratunac, again pursuant to your order, a total of eight buses from Drinatrans, two buses from their own military post, and four of our own trucks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again. Remind us what 440 was again.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: 440 was the Drina Corps order which specified that the Zvornik Brigade had to send a military police patrol to the checkpoint in Konjevic Polje by 1600 and that the Bratunac Brigade was to coordinate with the MUP on securing the Bratunac/Konjevic Polje highway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Anything else on that document?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. Most of the other information in this respect deals with their understanding of the growing threat in Zvornik posed by the Bosnian Muslim column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, we'll get to that a little bit later, but let's go on to the next exhibit which I believe is 451.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just before we get to that, I just want to point a correction. 440 talks about cooperation not coordination. I know it's minor, but the gentleman indicated coordination. My notes and I believe that the document will reflect, cooperation and there may be a distinction at some point that we would highlight during the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much. I think the coordination may be a big issue in this case, since we have heard it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document which is Prosecution Exhibit 451 is the 12 July 1995 report from the Main Staff of the Army of the Republika Srpska to the corps as well as to the president of the republic, outlining the daily activities of the army to the president.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did we get this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was provided by Colonel Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what's the significance of this document, in particular?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we can go to page 3 of the English language translation, starting in paragraph 6, this is the report reflecting the Main Staff's knowledge of the overall military situation in the zone of the Drina Corps. A, reflects the enemy situation. Subparagraph B reflects the situation in the corps, specifically noting that all Krivaja 95 tasks are going ahead as planned. It notes that during the day, they, being the Drina Corps, liberated Potocari, and they continue to advance in order to liberate all of the settlements of the Srebrenica enclave. It has and is somewhat unclear, on an unknown word, axis, part of our units and MUP units have organised ambushes in order to destroy Muslim extremists who have not surrendered and who are trying to break out from the enclave towards Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why is that reference important?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It again reflects the interrelationship between the army and the MUP and that the army is fully cognisant of what the MUP is doing and where their role is in the operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will we see MUP documents on the same subject that have a little different viewpoint of this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, we will.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just give us a preview of what that issue is about so the Court can understand, before we get to the document from the MUP.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: What will happen over the next 12 to 24 hours in the July 1995 perspective is that on the evening of 12 July 1995, General Mladic redirects large portions of the army forces in the Srebrenica enclave to disengage from the operations that they're involved in and to redeploy away from the Srebrenica area and to begin to initiate military operations designed to capture the Zepa safe area. This leaves, as time goes by, less and less army forces in the area to deal with the growing threat of the column, and it leaves the police forces to deal with that same threat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. As we get into documents related to that area, we'll discuss it specifically, and specifically you do have documents related to the Bratunac Brigade's role in these events?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. What else, if anything, from this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: On paragraph -- or number 2, situation on the territory, the Main Staff reporting to the president of the republic the information that 10.000 Muslims are estimated for transport. And in all areas -- that sentence, we'll just leave it at that. That is almost a direct read, that number 10.000, from the previous 12 July report from the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. An indication of how the reporting chain goes from the brigade level to the Main Staff and of on items of significance or interest to the president of the republic. The last thing I'd like to highlight on this document is the signature, and as I've previously testified, reflecting that on 12 July 1995, Major General Miletic is functioning as the acting chief of staff of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say "signature," but is that what you meant?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the signature block. We do not -- because this is an electronic version, we do not have his physical signature on the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what's the next document for 12 July?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a 12 July 1995 intelligence report from the Zvornik Infantry Brigade intelligence organ to the Drina Corps command intelligence section, reflecting the intelligence officer's view of the situation in his zone, notes that he's keeping his brigade chief of staff and another individual, the commander of the Tactical Group Osmaci informed of the situation, as he understands it. And towards the bottom of that rather large paragraph, it notes that based on radio intercepts, who are talking on the same frequency, they're following events of the column, it notes that they are fleeing in panic without any control, in groups or individually, and giving themselves up to the MUP or the VRS. So notwithstanding the actual information that they have on the column, this document indicates, again, the common knowledge that prisoners in the hundreds are being taken by the army and the MUP, and that it is an issue of general awareness throughout the region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the next document? I believe it's 453.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. This is the last document, I believe, for 12 July 1995. And this is from the command of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade to the command of the 1st Milici Light Infantry Brigade requesting that they be informed by midnight where their forces are deployed on their left flank with respect to us, the forces of the Bratunac Brigade, and regarding the gap between us, which the column is passing through. As you can tell, this document in fact does not go out until 15 minutes after midnight on the 13th. And it is typed signed for Colonel Blagojevic, and on the handwritten copy there is no indication of who might have signed the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, in the military context when documents like this and documents like the daily combat report go out under the name of the commander, in this case Blagojevic, even in cases where the commander doesn't sign it, is the commander supposed to know about the information that's in such reports that go out under his name? How does that work in a military context?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly in a general military context, if a report goes out under a commander's name, it is assumed that the commander is aware of the contents of that report. More specifically, even to the VRS, in 1994 there are a series of instructions from the Main Staff, and I have to say that I have not included those as a part of my narrative, because I didn't believe this was an area that was going to be discussed, so I can provide the documents if they are required, there are issues where the Main Staff is making directives to ensure that when daily combat reports go out, that the commanders are aware of the contents of them, and if necessary, to see them personal. That is a normal military practice, to my knowledge, if a document goes out under the commander's name, he is expected to be aware of the contents of that document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your review of the daily combat reports for this time period, and I don't expect exact numbers on this, but how often do you see the derogatory terms for Muslim, such as "Poturice and Turks," or "Turkish population," things like that, on the official daily combat reports?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a consistent feature, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next -- I think we're now getting into 13 July, and I think you have set the scene for us briefly, and I know this Court has heard lots of evidence on these dates, so I don't think we need to go into it in detail. So if you could, let's start with this exhibit, which has the correct number on it which is P203, an intercept from 13 July at 0700, which I know this Trial Chamber has seen quite a bit of, so I don't want to go into a whole lot of detail on this. But is this an intercept that you have previously incorporated into your analysis for the Krstic trial?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And have you changed your analysis since that time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to this intercept, yes, sir, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if there's a request, we'll go to private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, you were telling us about your analysis of this the first time around with General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. As I indicated previously, my prior analysis of this conversation in the case of General Krstic was that the general was General Krstic (redacted) (redacted) . Based on evidence that has come before the Court, I no longer believe that that is, in fact, the case. And one of the reasons why I wanted to bring this out was to make it clear that in this particular case I subscribe to the interpretation that a number of witnesses have already given to this exhibit. And I guess it would be easier if I don't have to go into the details of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't think we need to go into the details of this anymore, either. It's been heard several times. All right, Mr. Butler, so let's go on to the next exhibit, that is Exhibit 207,13 July intercept.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular intercept you have one of the identified correspondents being Krsmanovic who, as I've indicated, is the transportation officer of the Drina Corps. And again, talks to somebody else while I find Krstic for you, and he ends up speaking with Krsmanovic. One of the things I like to point out is with respect to the intercepts that people should also be aware of is that the nickname of Krle is occasionally attributed to Krsmanovic as well. So in examining the intercepts, and in some of them we will have Krle as a nickname for General Krstic, again it's just something I'm aware of when I review these intercepts that it's not the sole use of that nickname and who it can be attributed to. One of the interesting things - and at this point I confess I don't have a logical explanation for it - is references in the conversation for, over there, you know, those in Batkovic. To my knowledge the only reference of Batkovic in any of this context is the prisoner of war camp up in Batkovic in the Bijeljina area. And it appears from looking at this intercept that there was discussion that at least one batch will go there. It says from Sekovici, but on the morning of 13 July, even at 1100 hours, my understanding of the movement of the column that there should not have been anyone from the column in the Sekovici or Birac Brigade area, which would lend to their being captured.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you again just point out, remind us where Sekovici is. We didn't put it on the map.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Birac area is this general area here, and Sekovici I believe is a small town located in approximately this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just roughly midway between it looks like Cancari and Tisca. We have other maps that have that more clearly labelled. All right. Anything else you want to point out on that subject or this intercept?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this intercept, it again reflects the fact that the Drina Corps officers are quite well-informed about the status of the movement of the Bosnian Muslims, reflecting that two turns have already gone by, they have another 5.000, and everything is full for two turns. So they stopped the movement last night and started again at 6.00 in the morning on 13 July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it says, I stopped at 0830 hours. Can that be correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, it's not. I believe that's 2030, given the context that it says, I stopped last night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: And at the bottom of it, again the reference that, We'll ask UNPROFOR for fuel. You can count on that. The final part of the conversation attributed to Krsmanovic, noting that the maximum amount of rotations that they can do are two per day. Now, he accurately also reflects that they're not able to do it last night as a result of security reasons. And certainly from other information that's available in both documents and in testimony before this Court, the security situation on the road starting the evening of the 12th would certainly preclude running buses down that highway at night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Meaning in particular what?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The evening of the 12th is when they started to have the first significant contact with Bosnian Muslim forces from the column near the road approximately near the Sandici area. So that would have effectively cut the road off for bus communications, particularly at night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What's the next document we want to go to for the -- so we get more into the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Prosecution Exhibit 456; it is a 13 July report by the RS RDB. And in this particular instance, the first paragraph is the paragraph of interest reflecting the general knowledge. Specifically, as I just noted earlier, it reflects that on the night of 12 to 13 July, members of the VRS and the MUP captured a large number of Muslim soldiers numbering over 300 in ambushes set up in the general Konjevic Polje area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Aside from this specific reference, do you have any other specific references to this many prisoners being captured that night?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I do not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any indication, if this is true, what happened to the 300? Any information that would follow on this 300 reference?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly not with respect to documents, but I believe that is Court is aware of testimony with respect to individuals who were on that road and will discuss -- who have discussed the process by which they were captured starting the morning of the 13th, collected in various areas and moved towards Bratunac during the afternoon and late evening of the 13th. Looking at it in the general context, these prisoners obviously would have been merged in with the continuing number of prisoners who were taken during the day of 13 July. They would have alternately been assembled from Konjevic Polje, would have moved to Nova Kasaba or Sandici which were the larger collection areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But for these 300 on the evening of 12, 13 July, you don't have any specific information on?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anything else besides this general outline of the -- with some specifics that you need to discuss?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go to the next exhibit. I believe it's 457,13 July, another one of Mr. Vasic's reports.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. This is a report -- well, it's not -- we don't have a stamp indicating when it was sent, in the context, it indicates certainly the morning of 13 July and reflects that at 0400 hours on the morning of 13 July, large enemy group was in contact at the Sandici and Konjevic Polje areas, and reflects the police casualties in that battle. It reflects that they have no cooperation or assistance from the VRS in sealing off or destroying the large number of enemy soldiers, so that a lot of problems can be expected until the operation is completed, because the MUP is working alone in this operation and both the area and the number of Muslim soldiers is large.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is that -- based on your knowledge is the MUP working alone?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly from within the context of Dragomir Vasic and the MUP forces that are deployed from Sandici to Konjevic Polje, it just so happens that their units were destined to bear the brunt of the military assault of the column. From his perspective, I can certainly understand why he believes he is working alone. In reality, when you look at the broader situation in context - and perhaps it's more useful to do -- the map here - while the MUP forces are holding the road from Konjevic Polje to Sandici and somewhat to the south, in the woods along the defensive lines you have the 4th Battalion and then the 1st Battalion of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. You have the 5th Engineer Battalion or the caretaker elements at the garrison as well as elements of the Zvornik military police in this area. And you have the military police battalion of the 65th Protection Regiment from the intersection area south towards Nova Kasaba. And of course, from Nova Kasaba south you have elements of the Milici Light Infantry Brigade. So I could understand in isolation, Dragomir Vasic feels his forces are alone and fighting the column entirely on their own, in fact in context they're not. Although, to be fair, his forces are receiving the brunt of the damage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the description you've just given us Bratunac Brigade forces play any role in the direction of the Muslims, where they were going? How does the Bratunac Brigade forces work into what the MUP are trying to do along the road?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As documents that will be published later in the day on the 13th and the morning of the 14th indicate, the Bratunac Brigade units will be directed to begin sweep operations. And if I again may go back to the map, what in effect will happen is that the MUP will maintain blocking positions, and the 65th Protection Regiment, the military police, will maintain positions along the road. And what is envisioned by the command of the Drina Corps and ordered at the Bratunac Brigade level is a series of movements by the Bratunac Brigade into the former air zone of the enclave from their positions in an effort to essentially sweep the remnants of the Muslim column out and away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "out and away," for the record can you tell us what direction --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Away from this particular area, away from the roadway and to push them out towards Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record when you say "this particular area," can you describe it so the record will be clear?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Essentially as the remains of the column from Susnjari and Jaglici to push them north-west towards Nova Kasaba and towards the Muslim lines and essentially they're sweeping their terrain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why don't you have a seat. You've used this term "Sweeping the terrain." What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a military context, particularly as its translated from the terminology of the former JNA, and I believe that I've discussed before, it's very much like the cleansing type of the terrain. What we're in effect referring to is a military operation that engages or pushes the enemy before you so that once your troops have passed an area, it is secure or at least that there are no significant remnants of enemy troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. We perhaps have time for one more document, Exhibit 458.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. This is a 13 July report from Dragomir Vasic, noting another meeting in the morning on 13 July with General Mladic where we, the MUP, were informed that the VRS is continuing operations towards Zepa and leaving all other work to the MUP as follows. It lists that the MUP are now being given responsibility for the evacuation of the remaining civilian population from Srebrenica, killing of about 8.000 Muslim soldiers whom we blocked in the woods near Konjevic Polje, and I'd like to just point out in this context that we're not talking in this respect as killing as anything unlawful. I believe what he is envisioning here is the legitimate combat operations of engaging and destroying this column. It notes this is going on and fighting the job is being done solely by MUP units. He also notes his previous orders which are securing all key buildings in the town of Srebrenica, controlling entry and setting up checkpoints. And he's requesting in paragraph 4 that special detachments of the -- or detachments of the special police brigade from Srbinje or Doboj be sent to Konjevic Polje and noting that they'll be informed of further developments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, again was this job being done at this time solely by the MUP?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to both the evacuation listed in paragraph 1 and the engagement of the Muslim column in 2, it was not being done solely by the MUP. In fact, the army maintained -- remained as the primary apparatus by which this was accomplished.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It also says at the meeting with General Mladic this morning, we were informed, et cetera. Do you have any documents or intercepts or any other reliable information indicating where this meeting was held?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, that might be a good time to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll resume at 9.00 tomorrow morning.
